items.followUp: Define a trigonometric ratio and write the ratio for sine of an angle.

rubric.why: The definition identifies both the sides being compared and the right-angled triangle.
rubric.description: Defines trigonometric ratios as ratios of the sides of a right-angled triangle.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for a complete definition; 1 mark if only the ratios of sides are identified, without specifying a right-angled triangle (or vice versa).

modelAnswer: The ratios of the sides of a right-angled triangle with respect to one of its acute angles are called trigonometric ratios.

items.followUp: What is contact force? Give one example.

rubric.why: This states the defining feature of a field force.
rubric.description: States that a field force acts without physical contact between objects.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that the force acts without physical contact.

rubric.why: Gravity is a standard example of a field force.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example, such as gravitational, magnetic or electrostatic force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example.

modelAnswer: A field force is a force that acts between objects without physical contact.
Examples include gravitational, magnetic and electrostatic forces.

items.followUp: Define kinetic energy and name its SI unit.

rubric.why: Potential energy is associated with an object's position or configuration.
rubric.description: Defines potential energy as energy possessed due to position or configuration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly linking potential energy to position or configuration.

rubric.why: These are the two commonly described types of potential energy.
rubric.description: Names gravitational potential energy and elastic potential energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both types.

modelAnswer: Potential energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its position or configuration.
Its two types are gravitational potential energy and elastic potential energy.

items.followUp: Define work and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Efficiency compares useful output with total input.
rubric.description: Defines efficiency as useful output divided by total input (often expressed as a percentage).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct ratio.

rubric.why: Power is the rate at which work is done.
rubric.description: Defines power as the rate of doing work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

modelAnswer: Efficiency is the ratio of useful output work to total input work, usually expressed as a percentage.
Power is the rate of doing work.

items.followUp: A force of 60 N acts normally on an area of 3 m². Find the pressure.

rubric.why: Pressure is defined as force per unit area.
rubric.description: Defines pressure as force acting per unit area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: The pascal is the SI unit of pressure and is equivalent to N/m².
rubric.description: States the SI unit as pascal (Pa) or N/m².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct SI unit.

modelAnswer: Pressure is the force acting normally per unit area of a surface.
Its SI unit is the pascal (Pa), which is equal to N/m².

items.followUp: State the equation that relates pressure, force and area.

rubric.why: Pascal's law applies to pressure applied to an enclosed fluid.
rubric.description: States that the law concerns pressure applied to an enclosed fluid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying an enclosed fluid.

rubric.why: The defining result is that the applied pressure is transmitted undiminished in all directions.
rubric.description: States that the pressure is transmitted undiminished and equally in all directions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct transmission of pressure.

modelAnswer: When pressure is applied to an enclosed fluid, it is transmitted undiminished and equally in all directions to every part of the fluid and the walls of its container.

items.followUp: What is meant by the kinetic energy of the molecules of a body?

rubric.why: Internal energy includes the microscopic kinetic energies of the molecules.
rubric.description: Identifies internal energy as including the molecules' kinetic energies.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning molecular kinetic energy.

rubric.why: Internal energy also includes molecular potential energy due to intermolecular forces.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning molecular potential energy or intermolecular forces.

modelAnswer: The internal energy of a body is the sum of the kinetic and potential energies of all its molecules.
The kinetic energy is due to the random motion of the molecules, and the potential energy is due to the forces between them.

items.followUp: Using the equations of motion, derive the relation S = Vit + ½at².

rubric.why: This gives the first equation of motion needed for the derivation.
rubric.description: Uses the acceleration relation to obtain Vf = Vi + at.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct acceleration equation or its rearrangement.

rubric.why: Displacement equals average velocity multiplied by time for uniform acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the average-velocity displacement relation.

rubric.why: Substituting the first equation of motion into the displacement relation is the key derivation step.
rubric.description: Substitutes Vf = Vi + at into the displacement relation and simplifies.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct substitution or equivalent simplification.
Award 1 mark for the correct final equation.

modelAnswer: Given: initial velocity = Vi, final velocity = Vf, time = t, acceleration = a, displacement = S.
From the definition of acceleration: a = (Vf − Vi)/t.
For uniform acceleration, average velocity = (Vi + Vf)/2.
Displacement: S = average velocity × time = [(Vi + Vf)/2]t.
Substitute Vf = Vi + at: S = [(Vi + Vi + at)/2]t.
